'''Wotapuri-Katarqalai''' is an [[Dardic languages|Dardic]] [[Indo-Aryan languages|Indo-Aryan language]] documented to have been spoken in [[Afghanistan]]. It is unknown if the language still has active speakers, or is extinct.<ref>{{cite book |last=Owens |first=Jonathan |chapter=Endangered Languages of the Middle East |title=Language Diversity Endangered |editor=Matthias Brenzinger |page=265 |location=Berlin, New York |publisher=De Gruyter Mouton |date=2007 |doi=10.1515/9783110197129.263 |quote=Two of the languages on the above list are probably extinct, namely ''Tirahi'', and ''Wot'' (Wotapuri-Katarqalai). Of the latter we can witness how the process of extinction has moved on inexorably in the course of the twentieth century. In the 1940s Morgenstierne reported that Wot was spoken in two villages in the Katar valley, one at Wotapuri at the confluence of the Pech river with the streams coming from the valley, one further up the valley in Katarqalai. 15 years later Budruss (1960) visited both villages, found no speakers of the language in the lower village, ''Pashto'' having completely replaced it, and in the upper one only a few passive speakers who remember having spoken the language in their earlier years.}}</ref><ref>{{cite book |last=Hakala |first=Walter |chapter=Locating ‘Pashto’ in Afghanistan: A Survey of Secondary Sources |title=Language Policy and Language Conflict in Afghanistan and Its Neighbors |editor=Harold Schiffman |location=Leiden, The Netherlands |publisher=Brill |date=2012 |page=78 |doi=10.1163/9789004217652_004 |quote=Aside from the often insurmountable difficulty of organizing linguistic expeditions into these areas, Fussman notes how quickly the Dardic and Kafir languages of Afghanistan have been overwhelmed by the outside world, such that within a few years of Morgenstierne’s expedition, Tirahi and Wotapuri, for example, had become dead languages (Fussman 1972: 4).}}</ref> The most recent documentation of its use was published in 1983, when it was proposed that the language was in use in {{Ill|Katar-qala|qid=Q127263195}} and unlikely to be extinct in {{ill|Wotapur|nl|Wata Pur (dorp)}}.<ref name=":0">{{cite book |last1=Ėdelʹman |first1=Dzhoĭ Iosifovna |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cHW_p3EYCA8C&q=gawar+dardic+people |title=The Dardic and Nuristani Languages |date=1983 |publisher="Nauka" Publishing House, Central Department of Oriental Literature, 1983}}</ref> In September 2023, there were just 3 senior male speakers (1 in Katar-qala and 2 in Quro) living in the valley reported to Sviatoslav Kaverin who was conducting field research there.{{Cn|date=April 2025}}
